verdicts.claim: Open Legal flags for the P0 gate: RL-001, RL-002, RL-012, RL-014, RL-016 to RL-025, RL-027 to RL-030, RL-035, RL-036.
verdicts.what_is_true: The line lists 20 rows: 19 are still Open (several 'until Orb picks'), but RL-030 reads 'Closed until final art', so the list is not even accurate. No P0 gate was ever recorded (no gate packet; handoff.md:6 last says 'P0 is in progress') while later-phase work went ahead. RL-012 and RL-020 still say 'rename before public' though the repo is already public as orb-combat-ex. Not checked: whether RL-020's Must edits were made, or each flag's own release merits (other claims).
proof: evidence/AC-265.txt: git show HEAD:docs/legal/review-log.md, status column of each listed row, ls docs/production, handoff.md:6, git remote
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A stale gate list suggests the project is held at P0 and makes 20 rows of mixed age look like current blockers, hiding which ones matter for the web build or a store.
verdicts.fix: Retire the P0 line. Legal reissues one open-flags list keyed by horizon (already-public, web, store) and closes rows whose condition is met (RL-012: repo renamed).

verdicts.claim: Never put a prompt in front of Orb: sessions run in bypass mode and write commands that never trip the built-in safety check.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is in force (commit 9631fc75). Its content, guarding every variable in rm -rf and telling the EP rather than waiting on Orb, protects Orb's PC and nothing a player touches. The records contradict each other: CLAUDE.md:13, DIRECTORS.md:7, playbook.md:19 and ADR 0002:11 say Auto mode, while CLAUDE.md:19 says bypass mode.
proof: evidence/AC-266.txt: CLAUDE.md lines 13 and 19-23 (no diff vs HEAD), DIRECTORS.md:7, playbook.md:19, ADR 0002:11, git log 9631fc75
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Filed as safety, it pads the safety record with dev-machine hygiene. The Auto-vs-bypass contradiction can lead a restarted session into the wrong mode.
verdicts.fix: Move to a process or machine-rules section and state one permission mode in CLAUDE.md, DIRECTORS.md, the playbook and ADR 0002.

verdicts.claim: Every risk has an owner and a mitigation, and the risk register is kept as a live document.
verdicts.what_is_true: Each of the 11 rows has an owner and a mitigation, but the register is titled 'starting set' and has not changed since 2026-09-28 (f9ec6ac6, 111b1a17). It has no photosensitivity, privacy, licence, title, rating or AI-disclosure row. DIRECTORS.md:510 also names docs/production/roadmap.md and gate packets as deliverables, and neither exists. The real release controls live in Legal's log and the build gates, not here.
proof: evidence/AC-267.txt: risk-register.md in full, git log -- docs/production/, a grep for safety topics (none)
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Readers may take the register as the project's risk picture and miss release risks tracked only in Legal's log.
verdicts.fix: Either retire the register and point to Legal's review log and this audit, or have Production add the release risks with owners. It is a governance document, not a safety control.

verdicts.claim: Only the EP changes git state (reviews, commits and pushes); directors edit only the paths they own, and every session runs in Auto permission mode.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is stated the same way in every cited source, and the many uncommitted director edits in the working tree fit it. Who made each commit can't be checked, because one git user made them all. The committed Legal log lags the live one: HEAD has no RL-247 row (a HOLD on Orb's bystander decisions) and leaves RL-248 to RL-255 below the detail section. 'Auto mode' conflicts with CLAUDE.md:19, which says 'bypass mode'.
proof: evidence/AC-268.txt: the rule lines, git diff --stat HEAD -- docs/legal/review-log.md (9+/8-), row line numbers in HEAD vs working tree, RL-247 status
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Filing a workflow rule as safety adds noise. The public repo's Legal log is one held row behind the live copy, which has no player effect.
verdicts.fix: Keep as process. The EP commits Legal's reordered log with RL-247, and fixes the Auto/bypass wording.

verdicts.claim: Combat's CC-007 to CC-013 were never added to the register, and the register-agreement check is meant to fail until entries are added.
verdicts.what_is_true: It is true that CC-007 to CC-013 were never added, but the register covers the retired JS prototype (prototype/index.html at 7233c96), not the shipped Godot game. The agreement check passes today and fails only once a KB-007+ entry is added without a matching check, so the claim has it backwards. move-grammar.md already tracks CC-007 to CC-011, and CC-009 is marked resolved there.
proof: evidence/AC-269.txt: the check's parsing logic replayed on HEAD qa/known-bugs.md (6 confirmed entries, wanted=[], stale=[]); grep of CC-007..013
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It suggests an open QA failure and unscreened bugs in the product, when it is backlog against a retired prototype.
verdicts.fix: Retire the note, or point it to Combat's move-grammar.md list. Not a safety record.

verdicts.claim: LAN version 1 is 'Ready, not started' and must not run until Orb says so, because the firewall step needs Orb's real yes.
key_sources: docs/ep/vision.md (block 'Morning build and the first LAN match', 2026-11-07)
verdicts.what_is_true: The committed docs (last touched by a8bc66e2) still say LAN v1 has never run, but vision.md records Orb on 2026-11-07: 'both lan tests worked right out of the box', plus a first 2v2 with Orb 2. So the condition was met and the record is stale. The firewall step (one inbound UDP 47100 rule limited to the /24, removed afterwards) really does protect Orb's PC, at private horizon only. Not checked in code: whether the LAN kit is off in public builds.
proof: evidence/AC-270.txt: lan-v1.md:3,45,51; two-v-two-lan.md:12,50; git log; grep of vision.md for the LAN play; lan-n4 README:1
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A stale 'never run' condition makes LAN play look unapproved and can stall Netcode's next step. No player is at risk.
verdicts.fix: Netcode marks lan-v1.md and two-v-two-lan.md as played on 2026-11-07 on Orb's word and keeps the remove-the-rule step. Not a safety record.

verdicts.claim: Netcode exceeded its CPU cap (about 4 CPU-hours against 3), including a run at normal priority as a fourth Godot job.
verdicts.what_is_true: The self-report says exactly this (commit 9b111d15): 3.6 to 4.7 CPU-hours against 3, a 9-minute run that started without its arguments, and parity.gd for about 5 minutes at normal priority as a 4th Godot job. It also says nothing was left running. It is a machine-budget overrun with no player or release effect.
proof: evidence/AC-271.txt: report lines 20, 157, 160-164 and git log
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Filed as safety, it adds noise. At most it costs one EP ruling.
verdicts.fix: Close it in the EP's process log and drop it from the safety records.

verdicts.claim: Old-PC test of the private build: same warning before play, Orb alone watches, home address only with a /24 filter and 45-minute self-stop, no forwarding or tunnel, nothing recorded, and no flash number from it counts.
verdicts.what_is_true: RL-224 sets these six conditions for a private performance test and is marked closed on the ruling. Condition (2), 'Orb alone watches', no longer holds for Orb 2: RL-253 and Orb's 2026-11-07 ruling let Orb 2 see what Orb sees. The network terms (home /24, no forwarding or tunnel) stand and protect Orb's home network. No public build is involved.
proof: evidence/AC-272.txt: HEAD review-log lines 246 and 467, vision.md last block
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It reads as a live safety condition, and applied literally it contradicts RL-253 and Orb's ruling on Orb 2.
verdicts.fix: Mark RL-224 (2) as superseded by RL-253. Keep the network terms as private-test logistics owned by Performance and Netcode.
verdicts.belongs_to: process (Performance/Netcode private-test logistics; Orb's own risk acceptance)

verdicts.claim: Legal reads the store page, trailer, screenshots and capsules before they go live, and every published asset gets its origin row first.
verdicts.what_is_true: The gate is stated in four Legal docs and is still open. No store page, trailer or capsule exists yet. asset-origins.md's file-by-file log stops at 2026-09-29, with class-level rows only (last change 0f137cac, 2026-10-05), and Legal itself says file-level rows are needed before a store build, so the backlog is real. The gate genuinely protects Orb from IP and disclosure exposure at a store; nothing enforces it beyond Legal's checklist.
proof: evidence/AC-273.txt: the four gate lines, asset-origins.md:19 and :47, git log -1 of asset-origins.md
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: None: this is a real store gate, correctly scoped to the store.
verdicts.fix: Keep it as Legal's store gate, and schedule the file-level origin rows before any store build or trailer.

verdicts.claim: The EP escalates every Legal flag to Orb, one clear question at a time, and directors never message each other.
verdicts.what_is_true: All four sources state the rule. But Orb handed flash decisions to the team on 2026-10-18 ('You handle this', vision.md:1458), and RL-253 (1) says flash questions are not to be put to Orb, so 'every Legal flag' is no longer literally true. Directors never messaging each other is a chain-of-command rule with no release effect.
proof: evidence/AC-274.txt: the rule lines, vision.md:1458, RL-253 (1) excerpt
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: As written, it would push flash questions to Orb against Orb's own instruction, or make the EP look non-compliant for not escalating them.
verdicts.fix: Amend CLAUDE.md:16 and playbook.md:14 to carve out Orb's flash delegation (Legal and the EP decide; Orb is informed). Keep it as process.

verdicts.claim: No phase closes until its exit criteria are met and QA, Production and Legal have signed off.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is stated, but no phase gate was ever recorded. docs/production holds only risk-register.md (no roadmap or gate packets), handoff.md:6 last says 'P0 is in progress', and 19 of the 20 P0 Legal flags are still Open while later-phase work ships. In practice the rule is not in force. Release safety actually rests on Legal's per-item rows and the public-build gates.
proof: evidence/AC-275.txt: the rule lines, ls docs/production, a grep for gate packets, HEAD review-log:270
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It implies Legal and QA signed off each phase when none of that happened, which gives false comfort about screening.
verdicts.fix: Either run /gate for the phases already passed, or retire phase gating in favour of release gates (web, store) with Legal and QA sign-off.

verdicts.claim: QA harness hard caps so a run cannot hang the machine: --capsec 900, --wall 300 s, --budget, and godot.js guard() killing by PID after 100 minutes. Scripts run at most 3 jobs, headless only.
verdicts.what_is_true: Traced at HEAD: guard() kills by PID after QA_PROC_MS (default 100 min) and wraps the spawns in masher.js. players.gd, masher.gd and records.gd take --wall and --budget, and downtime.gd hard-codes 900 s of sim and 300 s of wall time. masher.js and timing-edge.js default to 3 jobs, but godot.js runRecords defaults to min(6, cpus-1), so 'at most 3' is a convention there, not a limit. This is dev-machine hygiene with no player effect.
proof: evidence/AC-276.txt: git show HEAD of godot.js, masher.js, timing-edge.js, players/masher/records/downtime.gd
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: No player cost; it only inflates the safety count.
verdicts.fix: Move it to QA/Tools machine docs, and optionally default runRecords to 3 jobs.

verdicts.claim: Machine discipline: at most 6 Godot processes per session, never the same batch twice, stop only your own processes by PID, make sure test runs exit, start runs longer than about ten minutes at below-normal priority (measurements on a saturated machine are invalid), and start headless Chrome only through Tools' launcher with a time limit, below-normal priority and one software capture per session.
verdicts.what_is_true: CLAUDE.md states the rules, and the browser launcher enforces part of them in code (below-normal or idle priority, a CPU cap, a hard deadline). They protect Orb's shared PC and the validity of measurements, not players or the release.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: No player cost; it inflates the safety records with dev-machine hygiene.
verdicts.fix: Keep these under the process/machine rules owned by Tools and the EP, outside the safety records.

verdicts.claim: Token discipline under ADR 0005 (Pro plan, zero budget, workflows or ultracode only with Orb's per-task approval) still stands in CLAUDE.md and the ADR, although Orb ordered on 2026-11-06 that all token limits be purged.
verdicts.what_is_true: This is true and stale. CLAUDE.md:17 and ADR 0005:10 still require Orb's per-task OK for workflows (the ADR was amended only for the 2026-10-23 push), and vision.md:47 still says 'Pro plan only'. vision.md:1656 records Orb's 2026-11-06 order: 'PURGE ALL FLOATING TOKEN-RELATED LIMITS'. It is a spending matter with no player or release effect, and the machine rules are separate and still stand.
proof: evidence/AC-278.txt: CLAUDE.md:17, ADR 0005 lines 3, 10, 21-23, vision.md:47, 73 and Orb's 1656 order, handoff.md:94, git log of ADR 0005
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Sessions that follow CLAUDE.md under-use the budget Orb wants used, against Orb's direction. No safety effect.
verdicts.fix: The EP adds an ADR 0005 amendment for Orb's 2026-11-06 order and updates CLAUDE.md:17 and vision.md:47 and :73, keeping the machine rules.

batch_notes: 13 of 14 are process records filed as safety. Only AC-273 (Legal's store-page and origin-row gate) genuinely protects Orb at release, and it is a store-horizon gate (S2) with a real backlog: file-level origin rows stop at 2026-09-29.

AC-270 (firewall step) and AC-272 (home /24, no forwarding or tunnel) really do protect Orb's PC and home network, but only at private horizon. Both records are stale: LAN was played on 2026-11-07, and RL-253 supersedes 'Orb alone watches' for Orb 2.
The records contradict each other: CLAUDE.md:13, DIRECTORS.md:7, playbook.md:19 and ADR 0002:11 say Auto mode, while CLAUDE.md:19 says bypass mode.

No phase gate was ever recorded: no gate packets or roadmap exist, handoff.md:6 last says 'P0 is in progress', and 19 of the 20 P0 Legal flags are still Open while later-phase work ships (AC-265, AC-275).

The committed docs/legal/review-log.md (HEAD) has no RL-247 row and leaves RL-248 to RL-255 below the detail section. The working copy fixes both, but it is uncommitted (it was written before the baseline).
No external rules were relied on for this slice. No Godot, browser or harness runs; the AC-269 check logic was replayed in a node one-liner.
